t: Rome’s state from the expulsion of the kings in 509 BCE to Augustus in 27 BCE, ruled by elected magistrates, Senate and assemblies.
Its citizen army and Italian allies conquered Italy, defeated Carthage and the Hellenistic kingdoms, and took most of the Mediterranean.
From 133 BCE political violence and civil wars, from Sulla to Caesar and Octavian, ended in monarchy under Augustus.
dyk: In the First Punic War Rome, with little naval tradition, built fleets of a hundred or more warships at a time, and fitted them with a boarding bridge, the corvus, to win at Mylae in 260 BCE.
ev: Traditional expulsion of Tarquinius Superbus and election of the first consuls
The Twelve Tables set out Roman law in writing
Victory in the Latin War and dissolution of the Latin League
Hannibal destroys a Roman army at the Battle of Cannae
The tribune Tiberius Gracchus is killed, opening an age of political violence
Julius Caesar is murdered on the Ides of March
Octavian receives the name Augustus, beginning the Principate
